procedures.text: SOP-101: Before replenishing a low-stock product, check available stock, recent sales and existing open orders. A purchasing manager must approve the reorder quantity before an order is submitted. A proposed or approved quantity does not mean the supplier has received an order.

SOP-102: If a supplier delivery is late, check the promised date and contact the supplier for a confirmed ETA. Record the supplier response and assign a follow-up owner. Do not promise a delivery date without supplier confirmation.
SOP-103: For damaged customer returns, inspect and quarantine the items. Do not add damaged units to sellable stock. Record the product and return reason before arranging a refund or replacement.

SOP-104: When a warehouse count differs from the inventory system, recount the product and reconcile recent receipts, sales and returns. A warehouse lead must approve any inventory adjustment; do not silently overwrite the stock count.

alice_note: RESTOCK-101: Our ceramic mug SKU-MUG-01 is running low after a promotion. I proposed reordering 80 units under request PO-1048, which is awaiting purchasing-manager approval. I prefer handovers with stock situation, evidence and the next action owner.
alice_update: RESTOCK-101 update: the purchasing manager approved reordering 120 units of ceramic mug SKU-MUG-01 under PO-1048, replacing the earlier proposal of 80 units. This is an approval only: no supplier order has been submitted. The delivery date is not confirmed.
bob_note: RESTOCK-202: Bob is reviewing damaged returns of tote bag SKU-BAG-02 under RET-771. This is a different product and workflow. Do not include RET-771 in the ceramic-mug replenishment handover.
